newsitem.title: JAPAN: Hanwa Bank president to resign -- BOJ.
newsitem.headline: Hanwa Bank president to resign -- BOJ.

text.p: Bank of Japan (BOJ) Governor Yasuo Matsushita told a news conference on Thursday that the president of Hanwa Bank Ltd, Takeshi Shinkyo, would resign.
The Finance Ministry ordered the regional bank in western Japan to halt its business apart from deposit withdrawals on Thursday because the bank was unable to recover bad loans.

"The Bank of Japan believes that prompt measures to deal with insolvent financial institutions without delay will lead to the early rejuvenation of the functions of the Japanese financial system," Matsushita said.

He said the BOJ would promptly arrange a comprehensive resolution scheme to deal with difficulties at Hanwa Bank, in consultation with the Finance Ministry, with the aim of protecting depositors and maintaining the safety and soundness of Japan's financial system.
Matsushita said the BOJ would consider establishing a new bank to take over all the business of Hanwa Bank. Hanwa would be dissolved and liquidated, he said.

He said all deposits at Hanwa Bank would be protected and the BOJ would take all necessary steps to secure sufficient funds, including the extension of loans under Article 25 of the Bank of Japan Law, should a shortage of funds for deposit repayment occur before the business transfer.
Loans under Article 25 are special loans extended to financial firms which have very low interest rates and require no collateral.
"There is no need for depositors to be concerned, and we strongly hope that they act sensibly," Matsushita said.
The governor also said Japan would use its deposit insurance system to protect depositors while in the process of liquidating Hanwa Bank.

Matsushita said Japanese financial institutions had been seriously tackling their problem loans, and added: "Overall, the ability of financial firms to cope with problem loans has improved dramatically."

Asked whether the worst was over with regard to bank failures, Matsushita said: "Although I suspect some individual firms are facing difficulties, it is difficult to make a judgment about overall conditions at this moment."
The governor said Hanwa Bank's problem loans totalled 77 billion yen, according to an inspection conducted by the Finance Ministry since August.
The amount includes loans that are unrecoverable and those that may be very difficult to recover, he said.
He said the amount Hanwa would need for repayment of deposits would be decided after discussions with creditors.

Asked whether the BOJ would apply the same methods in case of future bank failures, Matsushita said: "If there are failures, we will cope with them appropriately on a case-by-case basis using the deposit insurance system and with the basic objective of protecting depositors."
He said the BOJ had been informed by the Finance Ministry that government financial institutions had been asked to help Hanwa's business partners so they would not experience difficulties.
